title: Exploring TikTok's Effect on Perceptions and Misinformation Surrounding Hormonal Birth Control [ID 698]
screen_reason: Conference-abstract content analysis of the top 100 TikTok videos tagged #hormonalbirthcontrol. Among the 20 videos whose direct purpose was public health education, 55% contained inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information: a quantitative share of items coded inaccurate with a stated denominator, so CONTENT applies. Only the abstract is available, so methods detail, dates and reliability statistics are missing.

estimates.measure_type: % of public-health-education TikTok videos tagged #hormonalbirthcontrol that contained inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information
estimates.value_raw: Among videos with the direct purpose of public health education (n=20), 55% contained inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information
estimates.denominator: the 20 videos with the direct purpose of public health education, out of the top 100 TikTok videos tagged #hormonalbirthcontrol ranked by likes and retrieved with the Apify application
estimates.definition: Video coded as containing inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information about hormonal birth control by three independent reviewers assessing focus, tone, source and accuracy; the criteria for accuracy are not described in the abstract
estimates.misinfo_def: No definition given in the abstract beyond the coding label “inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information”.
estimates.source_quote: Among videos with the direct purpose of public health education (n=20), 55% contained inaccurate, non-evidence-based, or misleading information, and 25% were evidence-based or had citations included.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Three independent reviewers; the abstract names PEMAT and DISCERN as the validated tools used for understandability and quality, but does not say what instrument or reference standard was used for the accuracy judgement, and reports no inter-rater reliability statistic
estimates.moderator_quote: Using the Apify application, we analyzed the top 100 TikTok videos tagged with #hormonalbirthcontrol based on likes, assessing their focus, tone, source, and accuracy.
estimates.notes: CONDITIONAL DENOMINATOR: 20 videos, not the 100 analysed. The abstract gives no share of the full corpus that was inaccurate, and 55% of 20 is 11 videos, so the estimate rests on a very small n. Also unresolved from an abstract alone: no data-collection date or publication year appears anywhere in the text, so year is left blank rather than guessed; no country is stated, so country_norm is Global under the “worldwide/unspecified” rule, though the venue and framing suggest a US study. 55% and 25% do not sum to 100, so a residual 20% of the 20 videos fell in neither category. Rank-truncated hashtag sample (top 100 by likes), hence denom_selection=curated. Confidence low: abstract-only, tiny denominator, undocumented accuracy instrument, no reliability statistic.

missed_or_uncertain: Abstract-only text; the full methods and results were not available. NOT extracted: (1) “25% were evidence-based or had citations included”: the accurate share of the same 20 videos, not a misinformation share, and not the complement of the 55%. (2) Average PEMAT understandability 52%, PEMAT actionability 20% and DISCERN 32: scale means with no share of items, so QUALITY with no extractable proportion; the abstract states these indicate poor quality but gives no distribution. (3) Corpus composition counts out of the top 100 videos (created by patients n=50; personal experiences n=43; focused on educating and informing patients n=46; encouraging patients to decline hormonal birth control n=50): stance and authorship attributes, not veracity judgements. Note in particular that “most encouraging patients to decline hormonal birth control (n=50)” is a stance measure and must not be read as a misinformation rate. (4) No corpus-wide inaccuracy share is reported for the full 100 videos; the abstract's conclusion that “a substantial proportion of TikTok videos related to hormonal birth control present misleading information” is not quantified and cannot be turned into a value. FOR AN ADJUDICATOR: if a full text becomes available it should be re-extracted, since a 100-video denominator figure and the reliability statistics may exist there.

rob.design: Conference abstract (no full text available). Cross-sectional content analysis of the top 100 TikTok videos tagged #hormonalbirthcontrol, ranked by likes and retrieved with the Apify application; no collection dates, no country, no exclusion criteria and no video-level characteristics are reported. Three independent reviewers assessed focus, tone, source and accuracy and applied PEMAT and DISCERN for understandability and quality. No inter-rater reliability statistic, no accuracy reference standard, no funding or conflict statement, and no denominator for the corpus-wide inaccuracy rate. The reported inaccuracy share rests on a subgroup of 20 videos.
